questions.q: Which Python package handles authentication for Foundry SDK clients?
questions.explain: azure-identity provides credential classes like DefaultAzureCredential, which handle authentication without a hardcoded key.

questions.q: Where do you find the endpoint URL and key that Foundry SDK clients need?
options: In the Python package's documentation only
Your project's Overview page in the Foundry portal
They are not needed for any SDK client
questions.explain: The project's Overview page in the Foundry portal displays the Azure AI model inference endpoint and the credentials needed to connect.

questions.q: What does DefaultAzureCredential do that avoids hardcoding a key in your code?
options: It generates a new Azure subscription automatically
It tries multiple authentication methods in order — CLI login, managed identity, environment variables — until one works
It stores your password in plain text in the project
questions.explain: DefaultAzureCredential tries several authentication methods in sequence, so the same code works locally (via az login) and in production (via managed identity) without a hardcoded key.

questions.q: When calling chat.completions.create through the Foundry SDK, what should you pass as the "model" parameter?
options: Your deployment name, as covered in Lesson 3
questions.explain: Consistent with the Lesson 3 gotcha, Azure OpenAI routes by deployment name, not the underlying model name, even when called through this SDK pattern.

questions.q: What should you check if a deployment name throws a 404 or "not found" error?
options: The Models + endpoints page, which lists every deployment that actually exists in the project
Delete your Azure subscription and start over
questions.explain: The Models + endpoints page is the ground truth for exact deployment names in a project, which is the most common source of a 404 on a chat completion call.
